chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does the wife have a share of the blood-money (diyah) of her husband, and does the husband have a share of the blood-money of his wife?' He said, 'Yes, as long as one of them did not kill the other.'
ai.seo_question: Does a wife inherit her husband's blood money if he is killed?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that spouses inherit each other's *diyah* (blood-money) provided the killer is not the other spouse, thereby excluding the 'prevention of inheritance by the killer' (*mawnat al-qatl*) rule from applying between them. This ruling highlights the distinct jurisprudential treatment of spousal inheritance compared to other heirs, ensuring financial continuity within the marital bond even in cases of accidental death or non-spousal homicide. The condition 'ما لم يقتل أحدُهما الآخر' (unless one killed the other) aligns with the general principle that a murderer cannot inherit from their victim, a concept deeply rooted in both Sunni and Shia legal traditions.
